title: Night Lights, 2012–2023
blurb: City lights seen from orbit, and how they changed over a decade. Dark land and sea stay silent; every lit pixel rings.
hear: Bells mark bright pixels. Denser light means faster notes. North is high, south is low.

title: Sea Surface Currents and Temperature
blurb: Ocean currents swirling across the globe, coloured by surface temperature.
hear: Warm colours brighten the harmony, cool colours darken it. Flowing glass notes follow the strongest colour in each column.

title: GEOS Aerosols
blurb: Smoke, dust and other airborne particles from the GEOS model, each type drawn in its own colour.
hear: A still frame, read left to right like sheet music. Colour families take turns: the chord follows whichever colour dominates.

title: DYAMOND Global Carbon Dioxide
blurb: Carbon dioxide moving through the atmosphere in a high-resolution global model.
hear: A low drone thickens as the plumes brighten. Marimba notes trace where the gas is densest.

title: Lightning Seen from the Space Station, 2017–2023
blurb: Lightning flashes recorded by a sensor on the International Space Station.
hear: Each jump in brightness is a strike on the drum. The more flashes, the busier the rhythm.

title: GEDI Forest Height
blurb: Global canopy height measured by the GEDI laser instrument: the colour scale runs from low scrub to tall forest.
hear: Wooden marimba notes. Stronger colour means taller canopy and louder notes.

title: An Atmospheric River in 3D
blurb: A long band of moisture crossing the ocean, shown in three dimensions from an Earth system model.
hear: Sustained glass tones swell where moisture is thickest and thin out where the air is dry.

title: Perpetual Ocean 2: Western Boundary Currents
blurb: Fast, narrow currents such as the Gulf Stream, coloured by temperature.
hear: Plucked notes ride the bright threads of current. Movement in the frame drives the pulse.

title: Air Quality Model Runs
blurb: A frame from NASA air-quality model runs showing pollution in the atmosphere.
hear: A still frame scanned left to right. Bells sound where pollution is drawn most strongly.
